值得閱讀的理由

  • 梳理作者對國共合作及其對國民黨影響的批判性解讀，呈現他所說的思想、組織與革命目標混亂。
  • 介紹西山會議派反共主張的歷史脈絡，以及作者認為這些主張對國民黨具有的意義。
  • 呈現作者如何以革命理念、政治人物與歷史事件，論述反共立場及其後果。

摘要

國共合作與「掏心」之說

作者將國共合作形容為共產黨對國民黨採取的「掏心」策略，意指從內部削弱國民黨。他指出，國民黨追求的是三民主義與階級和諧，共產主義則主張階級鬥爭；在他的分析中，蘇聯式體制更是黨與意識形態凌駕國家及政府，將個人降為受支配的對象。

合作帶來的三種混亂

作者認為，孫中山被迫接受聯俄容共政策後，國民黨面臨三方面的混亂：第一是思想混亂，黨內同時存在信奉三民主義者與追求共產革命者；第二是組織混亂，共產黨員以個人身分加入國民黨，卻另行建立地下組織與派系；第三是目標混亂，國民黨所追求的民主憲政，與蘇聯支持的無產階級專政及暴力革命並不相同。

政治投機與革命方向的偏移

作者表示，國共合作削弱了國民黨，也替追逐名利與權力的政治投機者提供機會。他以金衛為例，形容其立場反覆，能因政治利益在親共、反共及反蔣等立場間轉換；並將這種現象與海外民主運動中的政治人物相提並論。作者也提到，自己近年主要專注寫作與研究，不願再投入他認為徒勞的海外政治事務。

在革命方向方面，作者指稱，國民革命軍與共產黨勢力在土地革命等問題上立場衝突，甚至發生對軍官家屬施以羞辱與批鬥的情況。他也以攻克武漢後，蔣介石遭親共派排擠、被解除職務並逐出黨的敘述，說明各方革命路線不同如何造成政治衝突。

西山會議派的反共原則

作者接著談到西山會議派，稱他們抓住了蘇聯與共產黨在思想、理論及行動上的弱點，並為國民黨留下重要的歷史基礎。他特別強調其思想反共原則：一個政黨不應同時奉行兩套指導思想；國民黨應以三民主義和民族革命為方向，而非共產主義與階級鬥爭。作者並引用其所述的理念，將中國傳統的仁義與世界民主革命的平等、自由、博愛，對照階級革命與階級鬥爭。

作者提出的歷史例證

為支持西山會議派的反共觀點，作者提出歷史例證。他先稱革命成功後，中國曾逐步走向和平建設、法治與社會平等，國民黨在訓政時期也給予一定言論自由；但他認為，這種自由在短時間內讓知識界大量翻譯馬克思著作、出版共產主義刊物，並使部分徬徨的青年受到革命思想吸引。接著，他提到抗戰期間延安的政治策略，指稱其主要攻擊對象是國民黨而非日本；不過字幕在此處中止，未完整呈現後續論述。

================================================

The Communists essentially waged a campaign of "heart-digging" against the Kuomintang. By "heart-digging," I mean digging out the very core of the KMT. We pursue the Three Principles of the People, not Communism; we want class harmony, not class struggle. The difference lies in the Moscow-style regime, where the ideology is above the state. The Party is above, the state is below. Communist belief is above, government is below. It is meant to turn a person into a mere object. Even lower than animals, lower than pigs, dogs, or cats. If you strike them, they will bite back. Mr. Sun Yat-sen. Forced to accept the Soviet-backed alliance with the Communists, it created a very harmful ... First. First, it caused ideological. chaos within the Kuomintang. In this party, you had people who believed in the Three Principles of the People and the national revolution, as well as those who believed in Communism and sought to carry out a Communist revolution. When there is ideological confusion within an organization, just think about what kind of situation that creates. This is. Second, organizational chaos. Communists joined the KMT as individuals. But they. established their own underground party cells. Then they built Communist groups and their own factional organizations. Exclusively to target the true Kuomintang members. And to co-opt those in the KMT who favored the Communists. With an organization in chaos, once a revolutionary organization is disorganized, how can the revolution continue? Right? Third, a confusion of goals. The goal of the Three Principles of the People and the national revolution was to establish the Second Republic of the Republic of China. It was to rebuild the Nanjing Nationalist Government of the Second Republic, to implement the Principle of Democracy, and to establish a democratic constitutional government. It is not what the Soviets wanted; what they aimed to implement, I don't need to say—everyone knows. Dictatorship of the proletariat, violent revolution, struggle, proletarian dictatorship. I said this many years ago. In the Soviet. theory of Communist revolution, there are three iron-fisted links. Namely, violent revolution and proletarian dictatorship. These three links define the nature of the Communist Party, and they have brought endless suffering to the people in all Communist countries. It was precisely under such circumstances that other consequences. arose. What was the first consequence? I don't know if the friends here are aware, but when I was young, I heard an old cadre say that when we were allied with the Communists, it wasn't really an alliance. The alliance was a "heart-digging" tactic against the KMT—digging out the KMT's heart. As I grew up, became a writer, traveled more, and met many.

high-ranking Communists. I would sometimes ask them. Was your alliance with the Soviets and the Communists back then just a "heart-digging" tactic? Did you not understand that? Because the Communists won, they dare to say anything; they won, so they don’t need to hold back. They absolutely wouldn't have dared to openly talk about their " tunneling tactics" against the KMT before '49, right? But after '49, they won, and whoever wins controls the political discourse. So they could claim it was a "tunneling tactic" or whatever they wanted. The KMT was indeed. undermined by them; this is not false. And it has continued right up to the present. Secondly, it opened up vast opportunities for political opportunists like Jin Wei, who hunger for fame, profit, and power. Regarding this person, I originally intended to talk about him specifically , but I didn't have time because I was writing. What kind of person is he? He is someone who loves fame, profit, and power. For the sake of fame, profit, and. power, he can abandon anything. That’s why he can be the Communist Party's best friend today and an anti-communist tomorrow. The day after tomorrow he’s anti-Chiang, and two days later he’s currying favor again. He agreed to join the Central Special Committee one day, only to issue a statement the next day claiming the committee was erroneous and reactionary. He is just that kind of person. It precisely provided those opportunists within the party, those with strong desires for power, with an opportunity. It is exactly the same in. the overseas democracy movement. People who haven't been anti-communist for decades now see the CCP about to collapse, and look at their antics now. They’ve gone crazy. The Republic of China faction is the same. So, for the past four years, I have only done two things: writing books at home from morning till night, conducting research , and doing necessary work related to the country. Regarding overseas affairs , whatever you tell me, I can't be bothered; it's meaningless. It’s been 31 years; I know everyone too well, I know this camp too well. And so, a person like Jin Wei just became popular like this. And what about the third point? The third point is that this forced policy of "aligning with the Soviets and cooperating with the Communists" caused. total confusion in the KMT's revolutionary direction. As I just said, it caused ideological confusion, goal confusion, and now, total directional confusion. Why, after the KMT's National Revolutionary Army defeated the warlords at the front, did the Communists within the army carry out land revolution, killing local tyrants and evil gentry, dragging out the mothers and fathers of the army's own officers—who were just small rural. landlords—to wear placards, be struggled against, and wear dunce caps? All of this happened. When the National Revolutionary Army took Wuhan, Chiang Kai-shek stood atop the Wuhan city gate , facing the incoming machine-gun fire without moving an inch. Those who followed him remembered it for a lifetime, saying, "The commander is, after all, the commander; he is not someone we can match." Yet, the Wuhan he captured was taken over by the Soviets and the pro-Soviet, pro-Communist.

faction within the KMT to establish the Wuhan government, and then they dismissed him as Commander-in-Chief of the National Revolutionary Army. They even expelled him from the party. At every stage, the differing directions of the revolution led to the horrors of the revolution. So, this was the situation faced by the Xishan Conference faction. In that era, at that critical juncture,. it was the Xishan Conference faction. They seized upon the Soviets’ ideological, theoretical, behavioral, and rhetorical vulnerabilities. And the vital weak points of the CCP. Because they grasped these vital points , they laid six foundations for the Kuomintang in history. What were those six things? The first is. the party principle of ideological anti-Communism. In the historical relationship between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party, the Kuomintang must adhere to the party principle of ideological anti-Communism. Because once a person's thinking is not anti-Communist, all their other behaviors will change. The Xishan Conference also proposed under this premise that one doctrine cannot hold two ideologies within a single party. Conversely, a party cannot have two. doctrines. It cannot have two guiding ideologies, yet the Kuomintang was manipulated by the Communist Party to have two guiding ideologies. The world would be in chaos. The party would be in great turmoil. These were their original words. It cannot have two guiding ideologies. Right? Therefore, the Xishan Conference faction made it very clear on this issue, stating that our goal is to launch a. national revolution against Communism; what we pursue is the Three Principles of the People, not Communism; what we want is class harmony, not class struggle. Clear, right? They also said something else, very well put. Revolutions in our Chinese history have always taken benevolence and righteousness as their direction and theoretical foundation; world democratic. revolutions also take equality, liberty , and fraternity as their theoretical construct. And as their revolutionary direction. How can one take class revolution and class struggle as the direction during a revolution? Even though our ancestors sought benevolence and righteousness, and world democratic revolutions sought equality. Violence occurred and blood was shed; if you were to call for class revolution and class struggle, what would the bloodshed be like? I don’t think I need. to say much more; the friends present here all know. What this class struggle and revolution turned into. Everyone understands. To be honest, these few sentences of theirs. I am convinced. For people in that era to say such things, it is truly remarkable. So. Let us use historical facts to prove the correctness of the Xishan faction, their correctness in ideological anti-Communism. I have four simple.

examples. First, after the revolution succeeded, China entered an era of peace . Although there was still sporadic gunfire, the nation was moving toward peaceful economic construction, law, and equality. Thus, even during the period of political tutelage, the Kuomintang allowed for civil rights and granted the people a great deal of freedom of speech . However, this freedom of speech was granted too liberally. And it happened too quickly, resulting. in a period of less than four years, from 1929 to 1931, where Chinese intellectuals and cultural figures actually had the capacity to translate all of Marx's works and launch dozens of communist publications to poison the minds of the youth. What was the result of this? Those young intellectuals, those who hadn't yet found their way in life, found that when their personal fates. were in turmoil, they were quickly swayed by communist revolutionary ideology. Desiring to go from slaves to rulers, they threw themselves into the flames of communism like moths to a flame. Second, during the War of Resistance, Yan'an was clearly focused on attacking the Nationalists rather than the Japanese, colluding with Wang Jingwei and reaching agreements with the Japanese to jointly target the Chinese. National Revolutionary Army that was fighting the war. Yet, many of our so-called "progressive " youth flocked to Yan'an. Why? Was it not because they had been bewitched by so-called communist ideology? Regarding the so-called Civil War, the new generation today doesn't view it as a civil war. The period from 1945 to 1949 was not a civil war. It was the second national war for the Chinese people in the first half of the 20th century. It was a new national war involving the Republic of China versus the Chinese Communist Party—led, Soviet-supported, joined by North Korea and Outer Mongolia , and incorporating surrendered Japanese troops. It is true, we were not defeated by any single entity. Furthermore, there was the final blow from the U.S. government. While the Soviets provided the Communists with $ 3.3 billion in. strategic investment, the U.S. at that same time revoked the $ 700 million in military aid it had previously promised to the Republic of China's government. The Communist Party was not fighting with "millet and rifles" alone; they were strong. The Battle of Taiyuan made it clear to the Kuomintang military that we were no longer a match for the Communist Party in terms of sheer military force. The Taiyuan I refer to is not the later battle, but the one. that occurred when the so-called civil war broke out, where the Communist forces and the National forces clashed— that is, between 1945 and 1946. This is something we all understand clearly, but do you know? Throughout China, our young students in universities could eat their fill of white flour buns, four dishes and a soup; my eldest brother was a student at Peking University, probably in the School of International Studies. He later became a very famous legal scholar.

Yet he said we were well-fed with four dishes and a soup, and then followed the underground CCP to go out and "oppose hunger." My brother told me this personally, and he also told the students in 1989 that he had to stand with them, saying if he didn't, he would betray his own conscience. Why? Was it communist ideology? Look, the children of high-ranking Kuomintang officials are not the same as the "red. second generation" and "red third generation" of the Communist Party. They were mostly well-bred and cultured, so why would they betray the Republic of China to join the Communists? Isn't it because the Communist Party seduced them with so-called communist ideology? Deluded them, and changed them. Isn't that the case? It is. So, how important are the principles of ideological anti-communism proposed at the West Mountain Conference? I won't even mention the 17 years from 1949 to the Cultural Revolution. Because the Communist Party's education was education in class struggle. It was education in communist revolution ; from a young age, they told us how landlords beat and killed peasants, and how capitalists abused the proletariat and working class, so our generation of youth was filled with intense, unforgivable class hatred toward. landlords and capitalists. That is why, when the Cultural Revolution broke out in 1966, those usually timid middle school, primary school, and university students could suddenly pick up axes to kill those so-called exploiters, use guns to execute the so-called landlords and rightists, and stand before their parents 'corpses to criticize their parents' reactionary. lives—what is this if not ideological poison? This is what communist ideological poisoning caused, which is why people overseas and in Taiwan are particularly interesting. Whenever they talk about the Chinese Communist Party being bad, they only bring up the Cultural Revolution. As if the CCP was only bad during the Cultural Revolution . People just don't know. The 17 years before the Cultural Revolution were actually the most vicious period of the Communist Party. The number of Chinese people killed or. persecuted to death by the Communist Party is conservatively estimated at 85 million, more than four times the number of Chinese killed or wounded by the Japanese, and most of it happened in those 17 years before the Cultural Revolution. Even counting the Cultural Revolution, even counting it... ...it was only 20 million people killed or wounded, which is one-fourth of the. 17 years before the Cultural Revolution . Without those 17 years, there would have been no Cultural Revolution. This is a point that we scholars who came out of China discuss far too little. These Western politicians don't understand at all; they are inherently arrogant and have no desire to understand the people of countries they deem backward. Regarding us, they only know about the Cultural Revolution; they think the Communist Party's only mistake was the Cultural Revolution, and everything else was fine.

We Chinese intellectuals who have come overseas should repent for this. As I criticized last time, mainland China has had 40 years of historical reflection, and today marks those 40 years of reflection. Reflection must first start with reflecting on the War of Resistance. I have given several speeches overseas about the War of Resistance, and though no one has refuted them, in 40 years of overseas democracy movements, not a single person or organization has held a meeting to discuss who actually fought that war. If you say the Communist Party fought the. war, or if you say the Kuomintang fought the war, they call you a liar; I have been called a liar right to my face. And I was even called a liar by your democracy movement leader, Yan Jiaqi, for saying the War of Resistance was led by the Chinese Communist Party. I am not saying he doesn't understand; I cannot blame him. Right? Many of us overseas think we are the smartest and most advanced because we stand on American soil. This American hillside is higher, so when I look back at mainland China, it's a lowland; therefore, all the. mainlanders are no match for me. Standing on this American high ground, I look down on my fellow countrymen in the lowlands and look down on them. I tell everyone here, do not do this. I came from the mainland, and when I first spoke about the Republic of China, no one overseas was talking about it, and my discussion of it was met with universal opposition. Everyone who makes a living off the Republic of China is actually against the Republic of China. In the democracy movement, all those who profit from the "Republic of China" label are against the Republic of China . Even those who were supported by the. Kuomintang for 30 years are against the Republic of China. The Xishan Meeting and the Xishan Meeting faction. They established a second principle of political anti-communism for the Kuomintang. The first party principle was ideological anti-communism; the second was political anti-communism. Why? Because it was the Xishan Meeting faction that. first realized that the future of communism is class dictatorship, that communist struggle is a life-or-death struggle, and that China's national revolution must absolutely not take that path, as it would be a betrayal of Dr. Sun.   • 梳理作者對國共合作及其對國民黨影響的批判性解讀，呈現他所說的思想、組織與革命目標混亂。
  • 介紹西山會議派反共主張的歷史脈絡，以及作者認為這些主張對國民黨具有的意義。
  • 呈現作者如何以革命理念、政治人物與歷史事件，論述反共立場及其後果。

摘要

國共合作與「掏心」之說

作者將國共合作形容為共產黨對國民黨採取的「掏心」策略，意指從內部削弱國民黨。他指出，國民黨追求的是三民主義與階級和諧，共產主義則主張階級鬥爭；在他的分析中，蘇聯式體制更是黨與意識形態凌駕國家及政府，將個人降為受支配的對象。

合作帶來的三種混亂

作者認為，孫中山被迫接受聯俄容共政策後，國民黨面臨三方面的混亂：第一是思想混亂，黨內同時存在信奉三民主義者與追求共產革命者；第二是組織混亂，共產黨員以個人身分加入國民黨，卻另行建立地下組織與派系；第三是目標混亂，國民黨所追求的民主憲政，與蘇聯支持的無產階級專政及暴力革命並不相同。

政治投機與革命方向的偏移

作者表示，國共合作削弱了國民黨，也替追逐名利與權力的政治投機者提供機會。他以金衛為例，形容其立場反覆，能因政治利益在親共、反共及反蔣等立場間轉換；並將這種現象與海外民主運動中的政治人物相提並論。作者也提到，自己近年主要專注寫作與研究，不願再投入他認為徒勞的海外政治事務。

在革命方向方面，作者指稱，國民革命軍與共產黨勢力在土地革命等問題上立場衝突，甚至發生對軍官家屬施以羞辱與批鬥的情況。他也以攻克武漢後，蔣介石遭親共派排擠、被解除職務並逐出黨的敘述，說明各方革命路線不同如何造成政治衝突。

西山會議派的反共原則

作者接著談到西山會議派，稱他們抓住了蘇聯與共產黨在思想、理論及行動上的弱點，並為國民黨留下重要的歷史基礎。他特別強調其思想反共原則：一個政黨不應同時奉行兩套指導思想；國民黨應以三民主義和民族革命為方向，而非共產主義與階級鬥爭。作者並引用其所述的理念，將中國傳統的仁義與世界民主革命的平等、自由、博愛，對照階級革命與階級鬥爭。

作者提出的歷史例證

為支持西山會議派的反共觀點，作者提出歷史例證。他先稱革命成功後，中國曾逐步走向和平建設、法治與社會平等，國民黨在訓政時期也給予一定言論自由；但他認為，這種自由在短時間內讓知識界大量翻譯馬克思著作、出版共產主義刊物，並使部分徬徨的青年受到革命思想吸引。接著，他提到抗戰期間延安的政治策略，指稱其主要攻擊對象是國民黨而非日本；不過字幕在此處中止，未完整呈現後續論述。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 梳理作者對國共合作及其對國民黨影響的批判性解讀，呈現他所說的思想、組織與革命目標混亂。
  • 介紹西山會議派反共主張的歷史脈絡，以及作者認為這些主張對國民黨具有的意義。
  • 呈現作者如何以革命理念、政治人物與歷史事件，論述反共立場及其後果。

摘要

國共合作與「掏心」之說

作者將國共合作形容為共產黨對國民黨採取的「掏心」策略，意指從內部削弱國民黨。他指出，國民黨追求的是三民主義與階級和諧，共產主義則主張階級鬥爭；在他的分析中，蘇聯式體制更是黨與意識形態凌駕國家及政府，將個人降為受支配的對象。

合作帶來的三種混亂

作者認為，孫中山被迫接受聯俄容共政策後，國民黨面臨三方面的混亂：第一是思想混亂，黨內同時存在信奉三民主義者與追求共產革命者；第二是組織混亂，共產黨員以個人身分加入國民黨，卻另行建立地下組織與派系；第三是目標混亂，國民黨所追求的民主憲政，與蘇聯支持的無產階級專政及暴力革命並不相同。

政治投機與革命方向的偏移

作者表示，國共合作削弱了國民黨，也替追逐名利與權力的政治投機者提供機會。他以金衛為例，形容其立場反覆，能因政治利益在親共、反共及反蔣等立場間轉換；並將這種現象與海外民主運動中的政治人物相提並論。作者也提到，自己近年主要專注寫作與研究，不願再投入他認為徒勞的海外政治事務。

在革命方向方面，作者指稱，國民革命軍與共產黨勢力在土地革命等問題上立場衝突，甚至發生對軍官家屬施以羞辱與批鬥的情況。他也以攻克武漢後，蔣介石遭親共派排擠、被解除職務並逐出黨的敘述，說明各方革命路線不同如何造成政治衝突。

西山會議派的反共原則

作者接著談到西山會議派，稱他們抓住了蘇聯與共產黨在思想、理論及行動上的弱點，並為國民黨留下重要的歷史基礎。他特別強調其思想反共原則：一個政黨不應同時奉行兩套指導思想；國民黨應以三民主義和民族革命為方向，而非共產主義與階級鬥爭。作者並引用其所述的理念，將中國傳統的仁義與世界民主革命的平等、自由、博愛，對照階級革命與階級鬥爭。

作者提出的歷史例證

為支持西山會議派的反共觀點，作者提出歷史例證。他先稱革命成功後，中國曾逐步走向和平建設、法治與社會平等，國民黨在訓政時期也給予一定言論自由；但他認為，這種自由在短時間內讓知識界大量翻譯馬克思著作、出版共產主義刊物，並使部分徬徨的青年受到革命思想吸引。接著，他提到抗戰期間延安的政治策略，指稱其主要攻擊對象是國民黨而非日本；不過字幕在此處中止，未完整呈現後續論述。

We pursue the Three Principles of the People, not Communism; we want class harmony, not class struggle. The difference lies in the Moscow-style regime, where the ideology is above the state. The Party is above, the state is below. Communist belief is above, government is below. It is meant to turn a person into a mere object. Even lower than animals, lower than pigs, dogs, or cats.
